key_insight: DARSM combines a physics-derived algebraic Reynolds-stress model with a neural network that predicts closure parameters, improving RANS accuracy and generalization without abandoning the governing equations.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical path to faster, more reliable turbulent-flow simulation for design workflows where high-fidelity CFD is too expensive.
method: Maps flow invariants to empirical parameters in an implicit algebraic Reynolds stress equation.
Derives the closure from Reynolds stress transport equations under a weak-equilibrium assumption.
Uses custom adjoint equations to optimize the coupled PDE-closure system efficiently.
evidence_signal: Across square-duct and periodic-hill benchmarks, the model cuts average test velocity error by 2–4× versus baseline RANS, with up to 12× improvement in individual cases.
watch_item: Training and deployment depend on a stiff coupled solver and custom adjoints, so implementation complexity and solver robustness are important practical concerns.
paper_title: Deep Learning-based Algebraic Reynolds Stress Closures for RANS Simulations of Turbulent Flows
